meta.title: SpaceRisk: ISO 31000 risk management your teams actually use
meta.description: SpaceRisk is an ISO 31000 risk register with bowties, barriers and monthly team reviews, a financial view for the board, ISO 27001 and other compliance frameworks, and a cyber programme built on real security findings.

hero.title: Every risk, from the team floor to the boardroom.
hero.text: SpaceRisk turns the risks your teams know about into living bowties, checks the barriers that stop them every month, and shows the board what it would cost.

sections.label: Risk signals
sections.title: Risk signals from your people and your operations. Clear updates for the top.
sections.text: Individuals and teams record what can go wrong where they work. Your plants, networks, cloud and identity systems add what the tools see. SpaceRisk gathers it into one enterprise risk picture and sends clear updates to the CEO and the CISO.
flow: Updates to the CEO and the CISO

sections.label: How it works
sections.title: The ISO 31000 loop, built into the month.
sections.text: No separate risk project that goes stale. SpaceRisk runs the standard as a simple monthly rhythm that every team can follow.

steps.title: Set the criteria
steps.text: One scale for likelihood and consequence, your appetite and your categories.

steps.title: Identify
steps.text: Teams and projects record what can go wrong, where they work.

steps.title: Analyse and evaluate
steps.text: Inherent, residual and target ratings, against the appetite.

steps.title: Treat
steps.text: Barriers and actions with owners and deadlines.

steps.title: Monitor and review
steps.text: Every month each team reviews its risks, checks its barriers and submits its return.

sections.label: Bowties and barriers
sections.title: See what stands between a threat and the damage.
sections.text: Each risk is a bowtie: the threats on the left, the consequences on the right, and the barriers in between. Barriers live in one shared registry, so one control can protect many risks, and you see at once when a weak one carries too much.
points: Preventive and mitigating barriers, with effectiveness and the date each was last tested
A Barrier Panel for the whole organisation, grouped by owning team or type
Escalation factors, and the barriers that protect the barriers

sections.label: Monthly reviews
sections.title: One rhythm for every team.
sections.text: Each month the team reviews every risk it owns and checks every barrier, then the team lead submits the return. You always know who is up to date, and the trend of every risk builds itself.
points: Team and project dashboards, with a heat map and the trend for each risk
Returns that can only be submitted once every risk is reviewed
A comment for every month, and a full history for the auditor
flow: Check every barrier the team owns
Add a comment for the month

sections.label: For the board
sections.title: Risk in the language of the board.
sections.text: SpaceRisk puts a price on exposure: expected loss, a simulated Value at Risk before and after barriers, and the return on what the barriers cost. The executive summary writes its own key messages and is ready to present.

boxes.d: As PDF or PowerPoint, ready to present.

sections.label: Compliance
sections.title: Two modules. One management system.
sections.text: Add the ISO 27001 module, the Compliance module or both. Each framework shows its loop with live progress and your next steps, and they share one set of registers: interested parties, legal obligations, objectives, documents, audits, management reviews, nonconformities, incidents and suppliers.
points: Each requirement shows the ISO 27001 controls that already cover the same work
Every framework exports to PDF, PowerPoint and Excel, and joins the executive summary
Overdue regulatory reports show on the executive dashboard

items.name: ISO/IEC 27001 and 27002
items.text: Clauses 4–10, all 93 controls, a Statement of Applicability, the ISMS loop and audit-ready exports. Includes the cyber programme.

items.name: ISO 22301 and ISO 45001
items.text: Business impact analysis with RTO and RPO, continuity exercises, worker consultation and the hierarchy of controls.

items.name: NIS2 and DORA
items.text: Incident reporting clocks, the supplier register and register of information, and resilience testing. With the Norwegian acts.

items.name: GDPR and ISO 27701
items.text: Records of processing, DPIAs and data subject requests with their one-month deadline.

items.name: ISO 42001
items.text: An AI system inventory with your EU AI Act assessment, and AI impact assessments.

items.name: Cyber Resilience Act
items.text: Products with digital elements and vulnerabilities, with the 24-hour, 72-hour and 14-day reporting clock.

sections.note: Guidance, not legal advice. Requirement texts are written in our own words.

sections.label: Cyber programme
sections.title: From security findings to a three-year plan.
sections.text: Upload results from the tools your team already runs. SpaceRisk turns the findings into evidence on the right ISO controls, finds the shortest attack paths to your domain admins, and suggests a prioritised programme on a transformation map you can take straight to the board.
points: Imports from PingCastle, Prowler and SharpHound
Findings, trends and fixes per target, across every run
Attack paths to Tier 0 from Active Directory data
A scored transformation map, exported to PowerPoint and PDF

sections.label: Agents and API
sections.title: Let your agents do the paperwork. People still decide.
sections.text: Scripts and AI agents get their own tokens and a documented REST API. They report and review risks, check barriers and upload tool results. In propose mode, every change waits in an inbox until a person approves it.
points: Every proposal is checked before anyone approves it

evidence.note: waiting for approval in the inbox

sections.label: Showcases
sections.title: 92 companies to explore, from banks to hospitals.
sections.text: Start in a world you recognise. Every showcase is a fictional company with its own teams, risks, barriers and history, ready in minutes. Each comes with a sample executive summary as a PDF.

sections.label: Pricing
sections.title: One yearly price. Every feature.
sections.text: Plans follow the number of teams that use SpaceRisk, from small organisations to the whole group.
points: Access by role: executives see everything, teams see their own, and money stays with the executives
Seven languages: English, Norwegian, German, Spanish, French, Italian and Portuguese
